title: Coffee Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Coffee Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Coffee nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in kape, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Coffee nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your kape (coffee) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, boron, zinc, magnesium, calcium, sulfur and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Coffee leaf turned pale yellow green all over, with only the veins a little greener, from nitrogen shortage
heroImage.credit: Tuesta Monteza et al., CoLeaf dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, zinc, calcium, sulfur and iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which coffee nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Coffee nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

Old leaves get a yellow band at the edge, then dark brown dead spots that join into a burnt edge. The centre stays green.
Muriate of potash 0 0 60, Sulfate of potash 0 0 50
old, lower leaves, between the veins

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of kape

New leaves come out small, bent and misshapen with dead tips, and the shoot tip dies.

New leaves narrow and strap like, yellow between dark green veins, bunched at the branch tip.

Young leaves turn bronze at the edges and cup downward. The shoot tip dies back.

Young leaves pale yellow, a little more along the midrib, but they keep their shine.

Young leaves light yellow to creamy white with a sharp net of green veins. Old leaves stay green.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a coffee nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest coffee nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in coffee

blocks.alt: Coffee leaf turned pale yellow green all over, with only the veins a little greener, from nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Tuesta Monteza et al., CoLeaf dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Leaves turn an even pale green, then yellow green, until the whole tree looks pale. In the Hawaii trial the young leaves paled first in full sun and the old leaves followed. Indian guides say the older, lower leaves go first. Leaves lose their normal glossy shine, old leaves may show whitish veins and drop early. Shoot growth falls by half or more. Flowering comes late and beans fill poorly. You see it most at this stage: any age, worst during new leaf growth and flowering, when uptake peaks, and on heavy bearing trees.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in kape
Trees that get little or no fertilizer, sandy or eroded soils with little organic matter, heavy rain that washes nitrogen down. Coffee grown in full sun, which uses nitrogen fast.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency also yellows young leaves, but those leaves keep their shine and the yellow sits along the midrib. Coffee leaf rust gives round pale yellow spots on top of the leaf with orange powder underneath, starting on the lower branches, not an even pale color. To be sure, send a leaf sample: on a lateral branch about halfway up the tree, pick the most recently matured leaf, usually the third or fourth pair back from the tip, from at least 15 trees, at or just before flowering, as the University of Hawaii coffee guide advises. Healthy leaves in the Hawaii trial held 3.0 to 3.7 percent nitrogen and deficient ones 1.5 to 1.9 percent.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 in a ring under the canopy and work it in, following the soil test. For a quick boost, Kerala Agricultural University gives a foliar spray of Urea at 10 grams per liter every 15 days. Yara puts the yearly nitrogen uptake of mature coffee at 150 to 250 kg per hectare. So split the soil dose over the rainy season.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in splits at the start and middle of the rains, keep a mulch and organic matter on the soil.
Phosphorus deficiency in coffee

blocks.alt: Older coffee leaf mottled yellow with an orange red tint between the veins from phosphorus shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Tuesta Monteza et al., CoLeaf dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: It develops slowly. Older leaves first show a faint mottled yellowing, then a soft yellow between the veins, and in bad cases dead spots. Indian guides also note a pink or purple tint on old leaves. Roots stay small, the tree grows slowly, and flowering and fruit set come late. You see it most at this stage: nursery and young trees after planting, and before flowering in bearing trees.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in kape
Acid soils that lock up phosphorus, and soils low in organic matter. A study of 22 coffee farms in Pigtauranan, Bukidnon found soil phosphorus very deficient on moderately acid soils (pH 5.6 to 6).
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen deficiency makes the whole tree pale, not mottled or purplish. Magnesium deficiency also yellows old leaves between the veins. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, plus a leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair on a fruiting branch. Healthy leaves in the Hawaii trial held 0.14 to 0.18 percent phosphorus and deficient ones 0.05 to 0.08 percent.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer near the roots, following the soil test. Superphosphate 0 20 0 acts fast. Rock phosphate and bone meal work slowly, as Kerala Agricultural University advises. The Bukidnon study suggests 16 20 0 and Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0. TNAU gives a foliar spray of DAP (Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0) at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) for a quick fix. Lime very acid soils, since phosphorus is most available near pH 6.5.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole, add compost or manure every year, and lime acid soils based on a soil test.
Potassium deficiency in coffee

blocks.alt: Coffee leaf whose tip and edge have died back dark brown while the rest stays pale green, from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Tuesta Monteza et al., CoLeaf dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Only the older leaves show it. A yellow band forms along the leaf edge, then dark brown dead spots appear on the edge and grow until the whole edge is dark brown while the area along the midrib stays green. Young leaves stay normal. Badly hit leaves fall early and branches can die back. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all while the berries grow and fill, when potash demand peaks.
Why potassium deficiency happens in kape
Sandy or porous soils and heavy rain that leach potash, heavy crops that carry potash away in the pulp. Heavy liming or magnesium that crowd out potash.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also starts on old leaves. But its spots are sunken and light brown in a wide band, with yellowing between the veins near the midrib. To be sure, leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair on a fruiting branch, at or before flowering. Healthy leaves in the Hawaii trial held 2.6 to 3.9 percent potassium and deficient ones 0.4 to 1.1 percent.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 to the soil under the canopy in split doses, following the soil test, as Kerala Agricultural University advises. For a quick fix spray Sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter with a sticker in the morning. Yara puts the yearly potash uptake of mature coffee at 150 to 250 kg per hectare, about the same as nitrogen.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash every year together with nitrogen, in splits during the rains, and return pulp and prunings to the field.
Boron deficiency in coffee

blocks.alt: Thick, leathery young coffee leaf with a notched, dead tip and uneven edges from boron shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Tuesta Monteza et al., CoLeaf dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: The youngest leaves come out light green, small, curved and leathery, mottled with small dead spots and with dead tips and uneven edges. The tip bud grows abnormally and can die, and the side branches show the same on their newest leaves. Older leaves stay normal. Flowers drop, fruit set is poor and beans can be hollow. You see it most at this stage: new flushes and flowering, often after a long dry season.
Why boron deficiency happens in kape

Soils low in boron, heavy liming, high rates of muriate of potash, and long droughts or very heavy rain. A Yara survey of about 16,000 coffee leaf samples found 29 percent below the critical boron level.
How to tell it apart

Calcium deficiency also damages young leaves and kills the tip bud, but the leaves turn bronze along the edges and cup downward. Zinc deficiency gives narrow, strap like leaves with green veins on a yellow background and short internodes, without dead spots and tips. To be sure, leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair on a fruiting branch. In the Hawaii trial deficient leaves held 9 ppm boron and healthy ones 31 to 52 ppm.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University gives Borax to the soil at 4 grams per tree, or a foliar spray of Borax at 1 gram per liter. TNAU gives a 0.2 percent Borax spray (2 grams per liter). Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizers in the same tank. Boron is toxic in excess, so do not repeat high doses without a test.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up, do not overlime, and add a small boron dose before flowering on soils that tested low.
Zinc deficiency in coffee

The youngest leaves yellow between the veins, at first just like iron deficiency. Later new leaves stay small and narrow, often strap like, with dark green veins, mostly along the midrib, on a yellow green background. Internodes stay short so leaves bunch into a rosette. Older leaves look normal. Berries can be misshapen and fruit develops poorly. You see it most at this stage: new flushes before and around flowering.
Why zinc deficiency happens in kape
High pH or overlimed soils, heavy phosphate fertilizer, and soils low in organic matter. Zinc is most available between pH 5 and 7.5.
How to tell it apart

Iron deficiency also yellows young leaves between green veins, but the leaves grow to normal size and shape and do not bunch. Boron deficiency also deforms new leaves, but with dead spots, dead tips and a dying tip bud. To be sure, leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair on a fruiting branch. Healthy coffee leaves held 18 to 25 ppm zinc in the Hawaii trial.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

In bad cases Kerala Agricultural University gives a morning spray of Zinc sulfate at 2 grams per liter mixed with 2.5 grams per liter of lime (calcium carbonate). TNAU gives Zinc sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter). Do not apply zinc on the same day as phosphate fertilizer.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid overliming and very heavy phosphate, and spray zinc before flowering where leaf tests run low.
Magnesium deficiency in coffee

blocks.alt: Coffee leaf yellow between a net of green veins from magnesium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Tuesta Monteza et al., CoLeaf dataset, CC BY 4.0, via Mendeley Data

blocks.text: Older leaves first go pale along the edges, then sunken, yellow brown to light brown dead spots form in a wide band along the edge. The leaf also yellows between the veins, most of all near the midrib. Leaves can curl or cup and drop early after a long shortage. Young leaves stay normal. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, mostly as the berries mature.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in kape
Acid, sandy, leached soils and heavy use of potash or lime, which compete with magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also starts at the edge of old leaves. But its spots are dark brown and join into a solid burnt edge, without yellowing between the veins. To be sure, leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair on a fruiting branch. Healthy leaves in the Hawaii trial held 0.30 to 0.35 percent magnesium and deficient ones 0.04 to 0.11 percent.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Kerala Agricultural University gives Magnesium sulfate at 32 grams per tree, placed in a band near the tree after a soil test. On acid soils Dolomite gives magnesium and lime together and keeps the problem away over time. Do not apply magnesium and potash fertilizer at the same time.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use Dolomite instead of plain lime on acid soils and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Calcium deficiency in coffee

Young leaves turn bronze, mostly along the edges, while the area along the midrib stays green. They do not open fully and cup downward. Later the newest leaves die and the tip bud dies back. Roots stay short and weak, and berries can be misshapen. You see it most at this stage: new flushes and while berries fill.
Why calcium deficiency happens in kape
Very acid soils, sandy soils that leach, and heavy potash or phosphorus, which push calcium out.
How to tell it apart

Boron deficiency also hits young leaves and the tip. But leaves are small, curved and spotted, with dead tips, not bronzed and cupped. To be sure, soil test for pH and calcium, and a leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair. Healthy leaves in the Hawaii trial held 0.94 to 1.16 percent calcium and deficient ones 0.36 to 0.55 percent.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

On acid soils Kerala Agricultural University gives 340 grams of lime per tree per year. Use Dolomite if magnesium is also low. On soils that are not acid use Gypsum. TNAU gives a calcium chloride spray at 1 to 2 percent for a quick fix on leaves.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils based on a soil test and keep potash and phosphorus in balance.
Sulfur deficiency in coffee

The youngest leaves turn evenly pale, with a faint yellow between the veins that is strongest along the midrib. Unlike nitrogen shortage, the leaves keep their glossy shine. New leaves stay small, internodes are short and shoots grow slowly. In long cases older leaves pale too. Fruit set drops and ripening is late. You see it most at this stage: new flushes and berry maturing.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in kape
Soils low in organic matter, sandy soils that leach, burning of prunings and weeds. Years of urea and muriate of potash with no sulfur source.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen deficiency also gives pale leaves, but the tree loses its shine and the old leaves yellow too. Iron deficiency gives a sharp net of green veins on a yellow or cream young leaf. To be sure, leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair on a fruiting branch. Healthy leaves in the Hawaii trial held 0.12 to 0.17 percent sulfur and deficient ones 0.04 to 0.05 percent.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency

Use a sulfur carrying fertilizer such as Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Superphosphate 0 20 0 in place of part of the urea. Kerala Agricultural University gives sulfur dust at 10 grams per tree on sulfur deficient soils, and Gypsum on alkaline soils.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep ammonium sulfate in the yearly program, return prunings as mulch instead of burning them, and build organic matter.
Iron deficiency in coffee

blocks.alt: Coffee leaf turned yellow between a net of green veins, an iron shortage sign on young leaves
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The youngest leaves turn light green between the veins, then yellow and finally almost creamy white. While every vein stays green and stands out as a clear net. The leaves grow to near normal shape but can be thin and small. Older leaves stay green. In bad cases leaf tips and edges brown, leaves drop and fruits stay small. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, most often after waterlogging or on limed spots.
Why iron deficiency happens in kape
High pH or overlimed soils and waterlogged soils. Kerala Agricultural University notes that low potash can bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency starts the same way, but the leaves turn narrow and strap like and bunch into a rosette. Sulfur deficiency gives an even pale leaf without the sharp green vein net. To be sure, soil test for pH and check drainage. Leaf test of the third or fourth leaf pair: the Hawaii trial found 1 to 25 ppm iron in deficient leaves and 43 to 61 ppm in healthy ones.
What to apply for iron deficiency

TNAU gives a foliar spray of Ferrous sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter). Kerala Agricultural University gives 6 grams of Ferrous sulfate per tree to the soil where a test shows low iron. Fix drainage where water stands.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not overlime, drain wet spots and keep potash in balance.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any coffee nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your kape needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Coffee nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my kape leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: the whole tree turns pale yellow green, leaves lose their shine and new shoots barely grow. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in coffee?
items.a: Apply Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 in a ring under the canopy and work it in, following the soil test. For a quick boost, Kerala Agricultural University gives a foliar spray of Urea at 10 grams per liter every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in coffee?
items.a: Apply a phosphorus fertilizer near the roots, following the soil test. Superphosphate 0 20 0 acts fast.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in coffee?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 to the soil under the canopy in split doses, following the soil test, as Kerala Agricultural University advises. For a quick fix spray Sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter with a sticker in the morning.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my kape lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the coffee nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
